About This Part
Volume 7B develops the infrastructure layer that supports production workloads in Microsoft Azure. Part A
established identity, governance, virtual-machine, and virtual-network fundamentals. Part B turns those
primitives into scalable compute fleets, segmented network topologies, secure application-delivery paths,
resilient storage systems, hybrid connectivity, backup, and disaster-recovery capabilities. The engineering objective is not simply to create resources. It is to define failure domains, traffic paths, recovery
boundaries, ownership, health signals, upgrade methods, and evidence before a workload is exposed to users. Every chapter connects design intent to implementation, validation, troubleshooting, security, and cleanup. Safety and Cost Controls

Use a sandbox subscription or an organization-approved training subscription. Verify regional availability,
quotas, pricing, and feature status before deployment.

Create budgets and expiry tags before provisioning scale sets, gateways, firewalls, Front Door profiles,
Application Gateways, VPN gateways, ExpressRoute resources, or recovery services.

Use managed identities and Azure RBAC. Never place credentials, storage keys, shared access signatures, or
private keys in scripts, screenshots, source control, or VM custom data.

Prefer Azure Bastion, private connectivity, and least-privilege network rules. Do not expose RDP or SSH to
the entire internet.

Run destructive operations only in approved training environments. Record cleanup evidence because
disks, snapshots, public IP addresses, gateways, backups, and replication can continue to generate charges

Standardizing VM lifecycle, images, availability, patching, access, and operational evidence

11.1 Production VM Design Starts with the Workload
A production VM is a managed operating-system boundary, not a permanent hand-built server. The
architecture must identify the workload process, expected traffic, data persistence, recovery point objective,
recovery time objective, maintenance window, administrative path, and replacement method. A VM that cannot
be recreated from an image plus configuration is a hidden single point of operational knowledge. Choose a VM family from CPU, memory, storage throughput, network bandwidth, accelerator, and licensing

11.2 Images, Configuration, and Drift
Azure Compute Gallery provides versioned image distribution and replication. A mature image pipeline builds
from source, applies updates, runs vulnerability and functional tests, signs or records provenance, publishes an
immutable version, and promotes that version through environments. Configuration that changes frequently
should be applied after boot by a controlled configuration mechanism rather than baked into every image.

1. Why should production VMs be replaceable?
Replacement removes configuration drift, supports deterministic recovery, and allows tested image and
configuration pipelines.
2. When are availability zones preferable to availability sets?
Zones protect against datacenter-level failure within a region, while availability sets separate instances
across platform fault and update domains without zonal isolation.
3. Why avoid secrets in custom data?
Custom data can be retained or exposed to privileged users and tooling; use managed identity and a secret
store instead.

Asset scope, health baseline, maintenance window, backup or rollback path, staged deployment result, patch
compliance, and post-change application validation.
5. How do you troubleshoot a running but unreachable VM?
Validate name resolution, routes, effective NSG rules, load-balancer path, NIC state, guest firewall, listening
service, and application logs in that order. Chapter Summary





14.2 NSG and ASG Design
NSG rules are evaluated by priority and use five-tuple fields plus service tags or ASGs. Because NSGs are
stateful, return traffic for an allowed connection is automatically permitted. Use subnet-level policies for broad
tier boundaries and application security groups to express roles such as web, application, and data instead of
maintaining fragile individual IP lists. A deny result is not solved by adding an unrestricted allow. Determine whether the packet reached the expected
NIC, which route was selected, which NSGs apply, whether the service is listening, and whether the return path
is symmetric. Effective security rules provide the merged result for a NIC.
14.3 Central Inspection and Egress Governance
A common pattern places Azure Firewall in a hub and associates spoke subnets with route tables that send
selected traffic to the firewall. Firewall Policy separates rule collections and can be managed across
environments. DNS proxy, threat intelligence, application rules, network rules, and logging must be designed

20.2 Azure Backup Architecture
Azure Backup uses vaults and workload-specific policies to create and retain recovery points. Design decisions
include vault type and region, redundancy, cross-region restore requirements, enhanced security, soft delete,
immutability, encryption, private access, identity, policy frequency, retention, and operational separation. Backup operators should not automatically have rights to alter production resources or delete protected data.

source and target regions, replication settings, target networks, resource groups, capacity, IP/DNS behavior,
dependency order, automation, test network, failover, commit, reprotection, and failback. A recovery plan
groups machines and actions in ordered stages, but application teams still own data and functional validation.
